title: A zero-work drag stall raises pericentre in a two-crossing Kepler orbit
abstract: We test whether drag cancellation can keep an orbit fixed during a period stall. For a bound Newtonian orbit with two opposite disc crossings, we prove that positive weak drag impulses with zero net orbital work must increase specific angular momentum and pericentre and decrease eccentricity and inclination. The gas can have unequal prograde azimuthal speeds at or below the circular Kepler speed. The result does not require a density law. We give a torque lower bound, a condition for small nonzero orbital loss, and a proof that an independent torque constraint removes the local two-impulse work ambiguity in the cancellation domain. An analytic identity passes 12,664 synthetic zero-work geometry tests. Independent vector derivatives and 1,000 exact sequential weak-impact cases check the calculation. For one synthetic case, a 1e-5 inner impulse raises pericentre by 0.084 percent while the exact final orbital energy stays fixed. This is not a fit or a new measurement of ASASSN-14ko. It shows that a drag-cancellation explanation of its clock must also account for changing tidal penetration or stellar structure. Sparse event times need not measure zero orbital work, and the proof does not cover mass-loss recoil, warped or eccentric discs, or full relativistic motion.
